title: Plan of Union — Unification with the South Georgia Conference
summary: The headline business of the session. After eighteen months of study by the Connectional Table, North Georgia is asked to adopt the Plan of Union that would merge the North and South Georgia Conferences into one new "Georgia Conference of The United Methodist Church." South Georgia votes on the same plan at its own 2026 session; if both approve, the Southeastern Jurisdiction is entreated to call a special session in summer 2026 to realign the boundaries, after which a joint Unifying Conference would organize the new conference for operation in 2027.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — presented by the Common Table.**

The North Georgia Conference is asked to adopt the **Unification Plan** (the full plan is published at [georgiaumc.org/resolution](https://www.georgiaumc.org/resolution)) with the intention that it govern the creation and structure of a new **Georgia Conference of The United Methodist Church**, with boundaries coextensive with the current North and South Georgia Conferences.

The resolution further entreats the **Southeastern Jurisdiction (SEJ) Conference**, at its 2026 called session, to:

1. **Approve the realignment** of the boundaries of the North and South Georgia Conferences to form the one new Georgia Conference;
2. **Authorize a joint organizational conference** — the *Unifying Conference* — consisting of the voting membership (lay and clergy) of both conferences, held before the new conference is formed; and
3. **Authorize the Georgia Conference to commence operations** as a fully unified conference once the Unifying Conference is complete, in accordance with the plan adopted by both conferences at their 2026 sessions.

Background: the cabinets of the two conferences met in July 2025 and deliberated consolidating into a single entity; both 2025 sessions had already voted to endorse the *intent* to pursue a new conference. This 2026 vote is the approval of the actual Plan of Union.
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — Common Table Report, Part 5 (The Resolutions), p.96

title: Joint Distributing Committee (Unification)
summary: A companion to the Plan of Union. Under Book of Discipline ¶1507, when two annual conferences merge, each must elect a distributing committee of three members and three alternates to act jointly with the other conference's committee. North Georgia is asked to affirm the creation of this Joint Distributing Committee with South Georgia and to approve its nominees, who will allocate pension responsibility and equitably distribute permanent funds, pension assets, and other property and liabilities between the two conferences.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — presented by the Common Table.**

The North Georgia Conference is asked to **affirm the creation of a Joint Distributing Committee**, together with the South Georgia Annual Conference, to operate consistent with **Book of Discipline ¶1507**, and to approve its three members and three alternates.

Under ¶1507, the joint distributing committee thus formed has power and authority to:

- **(a)** allocate the pension responsibility involved;
- **(b)** distribute equitably the permanent funds and all other pension assets of the conferences affected, taking the pension responsibility into consideration; and
- **(c)** to the extent not otherwise provided for, apportion or distribute equitably any other assets, property, liabilities, and obligations.

The committee is also authorized to act on plans and recommendations from the One Georgia Task Force and the joint working teams (health benefits, incorporation, legal structure) pending creation of the new conference, and is dissolved upon completion of its work.

*(The South Georgia resolution names its representatives: Board of Pension — John Ray; CF&A — Kathy Israel McLeod; Trustees — Jimmy Asbell; alternates Allison Berg, Jeff Cook, Precious Hawkins. North Georgia's nominees are presented at the session.)*
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — Common Table Report, Part 5 (The Resolutions), p.97

title: Election of Delegates to the 2028 General & Jurisdictional Conferences
summary: Reporting and balloting run throughout the session. The conference elects its clergy and lay delegates to the 2028 General Conference and Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference. Balloting begins Thursday morning with a voting demonstration and continues across the sessions until the delegation is complete; Session Six on Friday evening is a voting session held only if balloting has not yet concluded. The newly elected delegation meets immediately after Saturday's adjournment.
contentMd:
**Elections — balloting throughout the session.**

A central piece of the 2026 session is the election of North Georgia's **clergy and lay delegates to the 2028 General Conference and the Southeastern Jurisdictional Conference**. Clergy elect clergy delegates; lay members elect lay delegates, in equal number.

- Balloting opens Thursday with a **voting demonstration and Ballot #1**, and reporting/balloting continue across every business session.
- **Session Six** (Friday, 7:30 pm) is a dedicated voting session, *subject to cancellation if voting has already concluded.*
- The **newly elected delegation meets immediately following adjournment** on Saturday.

Self-nominated lay candidate information appears in the handbook (report 900), and a Lay Candidate Forum is held Thursday morning before the opening session.
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — Agenda & Bishop's Welcome; ngumc.org Annual Conference 2026

title: 2027 Conference Apportionment Budget
summary: The Council on Finance and Administration (CFA) presents a North Georgia–only 2027 apportionment budget of $10,663,773 — an increase of $169,842, or 1.6%, over the 2026 budget. It is presented as a North Georgia–only budget because members vote on unification at the same session; if unification is approved, a new unified budget would be developed by both conferences' CF&A teams and brought to a joint special session later in 2026 for 2027.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — Council on Finance and Administration.**

CFA presents for approval a **North Georgia–only budget of $10,663,773 for 2027**, an increase of $169,842, or **1.6%**, over 2026.

### The conference budget areas

| Area | Amount |
|------|-------:|
| I. Ministerial Support (episcopal office, communications, DS compensation, equitable comp, Board of Ordained Ministry) | $1,868,654 |
| II. Retired Ministers Pension/Insurance | $870,000 |
| III. Administrative Fund (AC session, journal, handbook) | $360,000 |

*(Areas IV–XIV continue in the report; full detail in the CFA Addendum.)*

### Why only 1.6%, and why "North Georgia–only"

CFA has reduced the apportionment burden for seven straight years (2020 −7.8%, 2021 −19.0%, 2022 −5.0%, 2023 −4.0%, 2024 −10.2%, 2025 −25.0%, 2026 −5.0%). The modest 2027 increase comes amid real pressure: the impact of church closures on collections, the conclusion of Lilly Foundation funding (June 30, 2026) that had supported regional developer positions, and the need to sustain existing-church and new-church ministry.

The budget is presented as North Georgia–only because **members also vote on unification with South Georgia at this same session.** If unification is approved, a new unified conference budget will be developed by both CF&A teams and submitted to a joint special session of both conferences later in 2026, for implementation in 2027.

title: Board of Pension & Health Benefits — 2026 Recommendations
summary: The Conference Board of Pension and Health Benefits brings its 2026 recommendations and the Comprehensive Benefit Funding Plan for conference action, setting funding for clergy retirement (CRSP, MPP, pre-1982), the retiree Health Reimbursement Account, and disability benefits. The 2027 budget reflects "fully funded status" as of 12/31/2025 (unaudited) for these plans, with the per-retiree HRA benefit capped at $3,600/year.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — Conference Board of Pension and Health Benefits.**

The Board brings its **2026 Recommendations (205.a)** and the **Comprehensive Benefit Funding Plan (206)** for approval. These govern how the conference funds:

- Clergy retirement plans (**CRSP, MPP**, and the pre-1982 plan);
- The **retiree Health Reimbursement Account (HRA)** administered through ViaBenefits; and
- Disability premiums.

The 2027 budget reflects **"fully funded status" as of 12/31/2025 (unaudited)** for the defined-contribution HRA funding and the pre-1982, CRSP, and MPP plans. The benefit per retired clergyperson is currently capped at **$3,600/annum**, with retiree-medical fund reserves used to offset the budget impact. Apportionments for pre-1982 were discontinued in 2023 based on the actuarial valuation of the liability.

A companion set of **housing-allowance resolutions** (206.a) is acted on separately — see *Rental/Housing Allowance Resolutions for 2027.*

title: Rental/Housing Allowance Resolutions for 2027
summary: A standard but required annual action. The conference designates an amount equal to 100% of the pension, severance, or disability payments received during January 1 – December 31, 2027 by each active, retired, terminated, or disabled clergyperson as a rental/housing allowance under Internal Revenue Code section 107. The actual amount a clergyperson may exclude from income remains limited by IRS rules.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — adopted under IRC §107.**

The conference adopts resolutions designating, for **January 1 through December 31, 2027**, an amount equal to **100% of the pension, severance, or disability payments** received from Discipline-authorized plans (including all such payments from **Wespath Benefits & Investments**) by each active, retired, terminated, or disabled clergyperson who is or was a member of the conference, as a **rental/housing allowance** for each such clergyperson.

This designation applies to payments arising from service to the conference, any local church, annual conference, general agency, other Church institution, a predecessor denomination, or any employer that contributed to such a plan as part of the clergyperson's gross compensation.

**IRS limitation (NOTE in the resolution):** the housing allowance a clergyperson may actually exclude from gross income is limited under IRC §107(2) to the *least* of (a) the amount designated, (b) the amount actually spent to provide a home, or (c) the fair rental value of the home plus utilities. Clergy are urged to consult their own tax advisors.
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — Addendum 206.a (Resolutions Relating to Rental/Housing Allowances)

title: Equitable Compensation Guidelines & Minimum Compensation
summary: The Commission on Equitable Compensation brings its guidelines and standards for pastoral support, including the conference minimum compensation, the accountable reimbursement plan, housing-allowance and parsonage standards, and the conference arrearage policy. The Equitable Compensation Fund undergirds the Discipline's guarantee of security of appointment — that every appointed pastor receives at least the conference-approved minimum.
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — report 207 (Commission on Equitable Compensation Guidelines)

title: Property Resolutions
summary: Property resolutions are taken up in Friday's afternoon business session. These authorize the disposition (sale, transfer, or other handling) of real property of closed and discontinued churches, which under the Book of Discipline passes to the conference Board of Trustees. The specific properties are presented at the session. (The Board of Trustees' own written report states it has no matters before the conference for vote; the property resolutions are brought as floor business.)
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — Friday afternoon business session.**

When a local church is **closed or discontinued**, its real and personal property is held by and disposed of through the **Conference Board of Trustees** under the Book of Discipline (¶2549 and the conference's trust provisions). *Property resolutions* authorize the conference's handling of that property — sale, transfer, or other disposition — and direct the use of net sale proceeds.

For North Georgia, net sales proceeds from closed-church property flow into the **Barnes Fund for Church Development**, with CFA/Trustees-approved distribution percentages (for 2025–26: BEAT innovative-ministry grants 5%, emerging-congregations grants 40%, ethnic-ministries funding 7.5%, church-property revitalization district grants 35%, Methodist Center property reserves 10%, contingency/lawsuit funding 2.5%).

The **specific property resolutions are presented at the session**; the written Conference Board of Trustees report (209) states the Board *"has no matters before you for vote,"* so these come as floor business.
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — Agenda (Friday, Session Five) + Conference Board of Trustees report 209

title: Resolution on Voting Rights & Civic Engagement
summary: A resolution responding to the U.S. Supreme Court's 6–3 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais (April 29, 2026) and a called June 17, 2026 special session of the Georgia Legislature to redraw district maps. Grounded in the UMC Constitution (¶5), the Social Principles (¶¶162–163), and the prophets (Amos 5:24; Micah 6:8), and naming the Church's own history of racial exclusion, it calls North Georgia United Methodists to lament the decision, advocate for voting-rights justice, and use and protect the vote.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action.**

The resolution recites that the **Supreme Court's 6–3 ruling in *Louisiana v. Callais* (April 29, 2026)** dealt a blow to the Voting Rights Act of 1965, permitting the dismantling of majority-Black congressional districts, and that a **special session of Georgia's legislature** was called for **June 17, 2026** to draw new district maps. It grounds the Church's witness in Scripture ("let justice roll down like water…" — Amos 5:24; Micah 6:8), the **UMC Constitution ¶5** (working to address threats to racial justice), and the **Social Principles ¶¶162–163** (rejecting laws that marginalize by race; naming equal treatment before the law and democracy as basic human rights). It names the denomination's own history — the racially segregated **Central Jurisdiction (1939)** — and Georgia's history of voter suppression.

**Resolved**, that members of the North Georgia Conference **lament** the *Louisiana v. Callais* decision and call on all North Georgia United Methodists to **advocate for justice in voting rights**; and

**Further resolved**, urging United Methodists in North Georgia to **engage their civic responsibilities — especially to use their vote**, an avenue historically denied to so many people of color and women.
source: 2026 NGC — Resolution on Voting Rights and Encouraging Civic Engagement (final, with line numbers)

title: 2026 Standing Rules
summary: The Committee on Standing Rules presents the conference's own operating manual for adoption in the first business session, and brings revisions for the year. Among them: a Standing Rules Working Group recommendation that the leadership sections of the North Georgia Standing Rules be rewritten to refer readers to the Book of Discipline, in anticipation of harmonized Georgia Conference Standing Rules. Standing-rule changes require a two-thirds vote.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — Committee on Standing Rules.**

The **Standing Rules** are the conference's own operating manual: they sit below the Book of Discipline but above Robert's Rules, governing how leadership is organized, who may bring business, and how the session runs. The committee presents them in the first business session (report 800) and brings any revisions.

This year's work includes a **Standing Rules Working Group** recommendation that the **leadership sections of the North Georgia Standing Rules be rewritten to refer readers to the Book of Discipline**, anticipating harmonized *Georgia Conference* Standing Rules under unification.

The Standing Rules also provide the **Consent Agenda** mechanism (Rule C.7) used to adopt routine reports without verbal action — see *How it works → Consent agenda.*

A standing-rule change requires a **two-thirds vote**.
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — report 800 (2026 Standing Rules) + Common Table Report, Part 7

title: Committee on Nominations Report
summary: The Committee on Nominations presents its slate of nominees to fill the conference's elected boards, commissions, and teams — presented for information on Thursday and brought to a vote on Saturday. The Discipline asks the committee to work toward inclusiveness across clergy and laity, gender, age, district, and racial and ethnic representation.
contentMd:
**For Conference Action — Committee on Nominations.**

The Committee on Nominations proposes the people who fill elected positions across the conference's boards, commissions, and teams (report 700). It is **presented Thursday** in Session Two and **voted Saturday** in Session Seven.

The Discipline asks the committee to work toward inclusiveness — clergywomen, youth and young adults, older adults, small churches, persons with disabilities, and racial and ethnic persons — and to balance representation across the conference's districts.

*(The full nominations slate will be added here from the conference journal.)*
source: 2026 NGC Handbook — report 700 (2026 North Georgia Conference Nominations Report)
